items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: I still play a little Jack Teagarden, I’ll play “Basin Street Blues,” or “I’ve Got a Right to Sing the Blues” or something.

ctx.x: Well I think probably there’s a lot of song composers that are very fond of you also, because I’m sure some of them have gotten some royalties out of all the records you’ve sold, because of the great arrangements you’ve written of their music.

It’s been fun because I’ve been able to do what I’ve done all the years through the band days and the big band days and playing trombone — I still play trombone, when I go out on the tours I’ll play a little Jack Teagarden, I’ll play “Basin Street Blues,” or “I’ve Got a Right to Sing the Blues” or something. And I still have great musicians in the band. And it’s fun to play what I call good music, but still done in a way that the people that are out there listening and coming to the concerts can understand and…

Well that sounds like a great way to wrap up. And I want to say on camera that I’m very grateful to you for making the trip down from L.A. also, with the things going on in your life and you’re busy, and I really appreciate your coming down. And I wish you all the best.
